544645|2026-06.headline: Park Medi World Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs.476 crore, PAT up 35% to Rs.89 crore; FY27 guided to Rs.2,080 crore revenue.
544645|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs.476 crore (+19% YoY) with EBITDA excluding other income of Rs.126 crore (26.5% margin) and PAT of Rs.89 crore (18.6% margin, +220 bps). PAT growth was attributed mainly to lower interest outgo after term debt repayment. Occupancy fell to 56% from 68% as 960 new beds (Bhatinda, Agra, Panchkula) entered the denominator. Management guided FY27 revenue of Rs.2,080 crore, EBITDA Rs.530 crore and PAT Rs.360 crore, and announced two acquisitions (Rudrapur, commissioned 2 August 2026; Zirakpur/Mehar, Rs.107 crore valuation).

financial_highlights.change: +20% YoY; vs 26.3% margin in Q1 FY26
vs 68% in Q1 FY26; FY26 was 64%

segments.name: High-end specialties
segments.commentary: Contributed about 62% of revenue, up 440 bps YoY from about 57%. Neurology about 14.5%, cardiology about 12%, urology about 11%, joint replacement about 9.5%, oncology 9-10%, gastroenterology about 7%.

segments.name: Newer hospitals (Agra, Panchkula, Bhatinda)
segments.commentary: Agra (commissioned Feb 2026) and Panchkula (commissioned Apr 2026) are ramping in line with plan; management expects no EBITDA loss, with first-year margins of about 10-12%. Mohali, the mature comparable, is at about 26% margin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: revenue Rs.2,080 crore (+24%), EBITDA Rs.530 crore (+25%), PAT Rs.360 crore (+32%).
EBITDA margin expected at 26.7-27% for FY27; PAT margin 17-18%.
ARPOB growth guided at 10-12% annualised for the next two years.
FY27 occupancy expected to moderate from FY26's 64% due to new capacity.
Bed count: 3,960 at Q1 end, 4,290 after Rudrapur (Q2), 4,740 at FY27 end (450 beds in Oct-Dec 2026), 5,740 by FY28 end.

CGHS rate revision (12-15% headline, about 7-7.5% net benefit to ARPOB, 70% of patients on CGHS) to flow fully from Q2 FY27; management says limited EBITDA benefit as it is redeployed into equipment and maintenance.
Payer mix target of 70:30 (government schemes vs cash/TPA) over 12-18 months.
Debtor days target of 125-130 days over the medium term.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 beds: 3,960 (up 32% YoY), including Panchkula's 350 beds; 960 beds added in last 12 months across Bhatinda (250), Agra (360), Panchkula (350).
Rudrapur (The Medicity, 330 beds, NABH) acquired for about Rs.177 crore all-cash; commissioned 2 August 2026. Additional capex of Rs.10-12 crore planned.
Mehar Hospital, Zirakpur (150 beds) acquisition at about Rs.107 crore valuation announced 3 August 2026; commissioning targeted November 2026.
Palam Vihar 'Park Platinum' 100-bed extension in Gurgaon (Rs.25 crore capex, about Rs.25 lakh/bed), taking Gurgaon to 750 beds; Naraela 200-bed insolvency acquisition on track for commissioning.
Agra: Rs.245 crore acquisition cost plus about Rs.7.5 crore equipment/upgrade.
Capex per bed about Rs.37 lakh currently; ongoing projects of Rs.767 crore for 2,130 beds over FY27-FY28 imply about Rs.36 lakh/bed blended, including acquisitions.
Ambala adding 200 beds, largely oncology-dedicated; LINAC planned at Bhatinda and Rudrapur.
demand_pricing: ARPOB rose 12% YoY to Rs.30,444; management says trend growth is 10-12%, versus 3-5% in the past.
Mature hospitals are growing 18-20% per management.
Management says patient footfall at the Park brand was about 9 lakh last year and about 2.5 lakh in Q1 FY27.
Patient mix at new acquisitions (Rudrapur, Zirakpur) expected at 75-80% government and 20-25% cash/TPA.
Management says doctor attrition at consultant level is among the lowest in the industry; no comparative data was given.
Management said it has not faced any CGHS-related pressure in oncology, citing vendor relationships.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue growth outlook given bed additions, ARPOB and occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 revenue Rs.2,080 crore (+24%), EBITDA Rs.530 crore (+25%) and PAT Rs.360 crore (+32%); mature hospitals are growing 18-20%. ARPOB guided at 10-12%, with hospitals above 60% occupancy at 30-31% EBITDA and sub-60% at 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Greenfield units (Panchkula, Agra) show EBITDA losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no EBITDA loss is expected; new units start at about 10-12% margin in year one versus 26% at Mohali, and blended margin stays at 26-27%.

qa_highlights.question: How will Rudrapur and Zirakpur ramp up, and what are their financials?
qa_highlights.answer: Rudrapur (330 beds, previously about Rs.55-56 crore revenue on 200 beds) targets Rs.100 crore revenue, EBITDA Rs.20-22 crore, PAT Rs.12-13 crore in year one, then Rs.140 crore, EBITDA Rs.35-36 crore, PAT Rs.21-22 crore. Zirakpur targets Rs.70-75 crore revenue at 25-26% EBITDA in its first year of operation, commissioning November 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Incremental capex at Agra and Rudrapur, and capex per bed given acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Agra needed Rs.7.5 crore of equipment and upgrades on top of the Rs.245 crore acquisition cost; Rudrapur needs Rs.10-12 crore additional. Management says blended capex per bed stays at about Rs.36 lakh on Rs.767 crore for 2,130 beds over FY27-FY28, including acquisitions, with Palam Vihar at about Rs.25 lakh per bed.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the CGHS rate revision on ARPOB and EBITDA, and whether oncology faces pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the CGHS revision (12-15%, October 2025) gives about 7-7.5% net ARPOB benefit given 70% CGHS patients, with full impact from Q2-Q4; the benefit will be redeployed into equipment and maintenance so EBITDA impact is limited. It reported no CGHS pressure in oncology, which is 9-10% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 bed guidance now 4,740 versus the earlier expectation, and is promoter dilution planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap versus the earlier figure reflects 250 new beds (100 at Palam Vihar, 150 at Zirakpur) not in earlier communication; 1,000 beds in FY28 remain intact. On promoter stake, it said the minimum roughly 8% divestment is due by December 2028, with no timeline given and equity raise linked to an acquisition.

risks_watch: Occupancy falling to 56% (from 68% a year ago) as 960 beds ramp; FY27 occupancy guided lower than FY26's 64%.
Execution risk on 1,490 beds added in calendar 2026 and 1,000 more in FY28, including Rudrapur (commissioned 2 August 2026), Zirakpur (November 2026) and Naraela.
Capex per bed rising with acquisitions: Rudrapur at about Rs.177 crore for 330 beds versus the company's historical Rs.34-37 lakh per bed.
CGHS revision impact on ARPOB (about 7-7.5%) with limited EBITDA pass-through, as management plans to redeploy it into equipment and maintenance.
Promoter stake must fall to 75%, about 8% divestment by December 2028, with no timeline given; a possible equity raise could follow an acquisition.
Debtor days target of 125-130 and the 70:30 government-to-cash/TPA payer mix shift over 12-18 months, both still to be delivered.
key_quotes: Q1 FY'27 has been a quarter of consolidation, growth and continuous execution.
We will be at 5,740 beds capacity by FY'28, funded largely through internal accruals and IPO proceeds, without recourse to any fresh debts.
We believe that densification gives a very, very durable competitive advantage in this business.
So, we believe ARPOB guidance going forward is 10%-12% in that band on annualized basis.
544645|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, capacity and doctor retention, but cautious and non-committal on specifics: management declined to give a case-mix target, an attrition figure or a promoter-dilution timeline, and gave a few answers that were vague or partly inconsistent (for example, the bed-count gap, and Q1 payer mix quoted as 77/10/13 and 77/23).

544647|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 32% to INR998.8 crore and adjusted PAT rose 75% to INR128.3 crore, though Q4 margin dipped to 20.9% on a one-time INR10 crore ECL provision.
544647|2026-03.overview: NephroPlus reported FY26 revenue of INR998.8 crore (up 32.2%), adjusted EBITDA of INR238.1 crore (up 37.6%, margin 23.8%) and adjusted PAT of INR128.3 crore (up 74.6%). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR265.6 crore (up 21.2%), but Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 20.9% from 24.6% due to a one-time INR10 crore ECL provision on two aged accounts; management said it would be 25% excluding this. International mix rose to 42% from 32%, lifting revenue per treatment (RPT) 13.3% to INR2,598. Management reiterated 15-20% revenue CAGR over three to four years and gave no annual guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted EBITDA (FY26, excl. ESOP and Saudi expenses)
financial_highlights.change: +37.6% YoY from INR173 crore; margin 23.8% vs 22.8%
+74.6% YoY from INR73.5 crore; PAT margin 12.8% vs 9.7%
vs INR54 crore in Q4 FY25; margin 20.9% vs 24.6% (25% ex-ECL provision)

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Network of 468 clinics vs 447 last year (per Q&A); majority of FY26 additions were captive units, with five to six standalone greenfield units. Management plans 40-50 gross new clinics per year, excluding large PPPs or acquisitions. Price point about $22 per treatment.

segments.name: Philippines
segments.commentary: 44 clinics, third-largest dialysis network there and now second-largest provider per management. Price point about $111 per treatment; standard national dialysis price rose 58% in October 2024. Plans 12-15 roll-ups in FY27; a recent mid-size acquisition had 600-800 sessions per month and about 15 beds.

segments.name: Uzbekistan
segments.commentary: Large PPP project won in 2022, described as ROCE accretive; two small new clinics opened in Karakalpakstan during FY26. Price point about $60 per treatment.

segments.name: Nepal
segments.commentary: About six centres; moved from an India branch to a subsidiary, so this is a reclassification and not incremental capacity. Management said to model it on India dynamics.

segments.name: Saudi Arabia
segments.commentary: 51:49 JV in investment phase; a INR3 crore share of JV loss was booked in Q4. Ministry of Health and Ministry of Defense dialysis tender is at EOI stage and expected to reach RFP in a couple of quarters. First clinic at Riyadh Hospital due to launch within two months.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 15-20% maintained over three to four years; no annual guidance given.
India: 40-50 gross new clinics per year; Philippines: 12-15 clinics per year. Forecasts exclude large PPPs and acquisitions.
No large price increase expected in FY27; RPT change to depend on geographic mix.
No capex guidance given; management cited INR500 crore cash and ROCE-accretive capital allocation criteria.
Saudi JV to stay in investment phase for the near term; clinic count not yet predictable.
Capex per bed: India INR10-11 lakh (payback 3.5-4 years); Philippines INR40-45 lakh (1-1.5 years); Uzbekistan INR18-20 lakh (1-1.5 years).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was INR165 crore vs INR116 crore in FY25 (about 50% higher), split roughly evenly between India and Philippines with some in Uzbekistan.
Guest base 36,981 as of March 2026 vs 33,076 (up 11.8%); treatments 38.45 lakh in FY26 vs 32.97 lakh (up 16.6%).
Saudi JV is 51:49; participative rights of the partner mean line-by-line consolidation is not possible, so results appear as a single share-of-profit line for now.
Uttarakhand PPP (two clinics) renewal in process; Andhra Pradesh renewal phase due later in calendar 2026.
Reformmed.AI monitoring application live in 50 clinics, to be rolled out network-wide over time.
demand_pricing: RPT rose to INR2,598 from INR2,292 (+13.3%), driven by international mix (32% to 42%), favourable FX (Philippine peso +5%, Uzbek currency +7%) and full-year effect of the Philippines price rise.
Management said CGHS India price rose 35% in October 2025 after 11 years, and Philippines PhilHealth rose about 58% in 2024 (corrected in the call from 40%).
Management expects more competition in the Philippines from global and Indian players, citing a long tail of about 550-600 unorganised clinics that it sees as a long-term consolidation opportunity.
Management said GLP-1 drugs would cut developed-market new patient additions by about 0.25% and have no material effect on the emerging-market TAM.
Management said NephroPlus holds about 50% of the organised dialysis market in India and that the Indian dialysis population will grow from 3 lakh to 5.2 lakh by 2029 (13% CAGR).

qa_highlights.question: What caused the INR10 crore ECL provision and in which geography?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a one-time provision on two accounts, both four to five years old, taken out of caution under a KPMG-ratified ECL model. It declined to name the accounts or give a geographic split.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Uttarakhand PPP contract be renewed, and how long does tendering take?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Singh said the Uttarakhand contract is under renewal tendering and still operated by NephroPlus. He estimated two to four months if the process runs normally, with possible extensions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi JV loss run rate and when does it become profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Prashant Goenka said the 51:49 JV shows a single share-of-profit line because the partner has participative rights. Management expects more clarity on consolidation in a year or two, and the tender stage means no firm timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin in the standalone India business fall while international mix rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Prashant Goenka said India carries platform costs (IT, business development, Philippines support functions) during ramp-up. He advised viewing the company on a consolidated basis and declined to give country-level data.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex per clinic and does the 40-50 clinic target include PPPs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave capex per bed and payback periods (see guidance), said the 40-50 India and 12-15 Philippines targets exclude large PPPs and acquisitions, and that the AOP includes only in-centre organic and roll-up growth.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans to expand into CKD prevention or other adjacencies?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Singh said there were no plans for adjacencies at present. Vikram Vuppala said the founders are keen on a CKD prevention platform for early-stage patients, which would feed the dialysis funnel.

risks_watch: Q4 margin reading of 20.9% included the INR10 crore one-time ECL provision; watch for recurrence in receivables and the AR-days trend.
Renewal of the Uttarakhand PPP and the Andhra Pradesh PPP phase later in calendar 2026; management said there is no 100% certainty of renewal.
Saudi tender progression from EOI to RFP and the JV's continuing losses (INR3 crore in Q4).
Rising competition in the Philippines from global and Indian players as prices have risen.
Standalone-level margins are diluted by platform and corporate costs in India; consolidated-only disclosure limits visibility on country economics.
544647|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and the platform model, but guarded on timing: management declined to give country-level data, annual guidance, or Saudi clinic counts, and described PPP and Saudi outcomes as dependent on government processes.
key_quotes: We will want to maintain a revenue CAGR guidance of 15% to 20% over a period of three to four years.
Margins reduced from 24.6% to 20.9%, due to a one-time ECL provision of INR10 crores.
So, the best way to look at NephroPlus will be at a console level.

544647|2026-06.headline: Nephrocare Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23.7% YoY to INR282 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 30.7% to INR65 crore and margin at 23.1%.
544647|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 23.7% YoY to INR282 crore on 13% higher guest count (38,262) and 13.3% more treatments (10.3 lakh). Adjusted EBITDA rose 31% to INR65.1 crore, with margin up about 120-125 bps, mainly from a 175 bps lower COGS-to-revenue ratio that management attributed to procurement scale. Adjusted PAT rose 41.7% to INR37 crore. Management reiterated 15-20% medium-term growth guidance, while the Saudi tender remains an investment-phase drag of roughly INR3 crore per quarter on the JV line.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (after ESOP and Saudi JV add-backs)

segments.name: Philippines

segments.name: International (overall)
segments.commentary: Contributes about 45% of revenue, up from about 30% a year and a half earlier. Uzbekistan is the only private operator, servicing about 1,800 of roughly 9,000 patients.

segments.name: Saudi Arabia
segments.commentary: First clinic at Riyadh Hospital operational in July; home dialysis started; medical operator licence obtained; tender RFI response submitted. Still in investment phase with JV losses of about INR3 crore cited by analysts; no tender documents issued yet.

segments.name: Kazakhstan
segments.commentary: Subsidiary incorporated in Q1 to evaluate Kazakhstan and Central Asia; no revenue or timeline yet. Price points around $75 noted in the market.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term growth guidance of 15-20% over the next three to five years maintained.

Tax rate of about 20% offered as a proxy for the year (India and Philippines at 25%, Uzbekistan at 0% if healthcare revenue exceeds 90%).
NIDA renal nurse academy first batch to begin training in Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex of INR44 crore towards centre acquisitions and growth, vs INR43 crore a year earlier.

Philippines acquisitions generate goodwill split into intangibles amortised over 5-7 years, adding to D&A.

Dialysis is a fixed-capacity business: about three cycles per machine per day; management says network growth comes from adding capacity, and clinics at about 85% utilisation need spare capacity for unplanned guests.
Management says the Philippines greenfield cost about 4 million per bed (referenced by an analyst) and declined to give acquisition cost per bed.
demand_pricing: India is still early in its dialysis market life cycle; management puts the organised (pure-play) share at about 20-22%, with 78-80% still hospital-run.

75%+ of clinics are in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities; India operates in 300+ cities across 25 states.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain is from international mix versus cost efficiency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said COGS fell 175 bps as a share of revenue, driven by taking India procurement scale to other markets and by utilisation and supplier terms, not only reuse counts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise YoY, and how did they move QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses fell 133 bps QoQ. Drivers were ECL provisions of 2-2.5% of revenue (KPMG-assisted model), public-company costs such as audit and legal fees, and upfront business development spend for new international markets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did D&A decline QoQ despite Philippines acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited RFID-based asset tracking that cut machine replacements (about 50 a month previously) and a one-time benefit, partly offset by goodwill amortisation from seven Philippines acquisitions late in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi breakeven path and cost exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi is a binary tender market with four clusters; management does not give clinic-count breakeven and said further investment will depend on tender terms. Tender timelines are uncertain, and the company may not win.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose country-level or same-centre growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined, saying it manages capital at platform level and that dialysis growth comes from adding capacity rather than same-store price and volume.

risks_watch: Saudi Arabia tender timing is uncertain (management cited one to two quarters or longer, and three to four quarters before clear visibility); the company may not win, and more investment may be needed depending on tender terms.

Other expenses are elevated YoY, driven by ECL provisions of about 2-2.5% of revenue, public-company costs and upfront international business development spend; watch whether the 133 bps QoQ improvement holds.

Depreciation and amortisation trend: the QoQ decline came from RFID-linked machine discipline, which management called a one-time benefit, while Philippines goodwill amortisation over 5-7 years adds to D&A.
Working capital: AR days fell to 101 from 121, but management said AR days will stay relatively high structurally given 3-4 month government payment cycles.
Price increases are lumpy (CGHS about 35% in October 2025, PhilHealth 55-60% in October 2024), so RPT growth of about 11% CAGR is not expected to persist.
No country-level or same-centre disclosure; investors cannot separate organic growth from new-clinic and international mix effects.
key_quotes: We began FY27 on a steady note, with Q1 revenues growing more than 20% year-on-year.
So, this is a binary market. You win one of the four clusters in the tender; you have a business. If you don't win, you pack the bags and leave the market.
So, it's not that the international growth is coming at the expense of India growth slowing down.
So, this is much more of an execution game around disciplined capacity addition while making sure that the network level utilization is continues to be healthy.
544647|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on the platform story, scale economics and Philippines/India execution, but cautious and evasive on Saudi Arabia timelines, breakeven and JV losses, and declined to give country-level, same-centre, capex-per-bed or unit-economics detail.

544658|2026-06.headline: ICICI Pru AMC Q1 FY27 PAT rose 23.1% YoY to INR965 crore on 18.3% YoY MF AUM growth and a mark-to-market gain in other income.
544658|2026-06.overview: Quarter-average mutual fund AUM reached INR11.17 lakh crore, up 1.1% QoQ and 18.3% YoY, with market share of 13.4% and second-place ranking. Operating revenue rose 17.6% YoY to INR1,564 crore, and other income swung to INR181 crore positive on June-end mark-to-market gains. Operating expenses rose 14.3% QoQ, mainly from employee costs, with ESOP charges now debited for the first time. Operating PBT was INR1,100 crore (+20.2% YoY) and PAT INR965 crore (+23.1% YoY). Industry SIP flows were flat-to-soft in the quarter and June rebounded, while the company said its own numbers track the industry.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 23% PAT growth and what helped in Q1 despite geopolitics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited resilient industry net flows and SIP over the prior year. Net sales were over INR4.6 lakh crore in FY26, and mark-to-market gains on the equity base also lifted PAT.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the change in market share, flows vs MTM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly share shifts are mainly MTM-driven given the high equity AUM base. Small caps returned 24%, mid caps 17.2% and large caps 8.9%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP cost and how should employee opex be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 ESOP cost is INR64-68 crore, charged evenly (not front-loaded). Management said the June quarter's INR200 crore quarterly opex is a fair base for modelling.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP flows fall and what is the ticket-size or stoppage picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the net SIP trigger fell because stoppages of older SIPs exceeded new SIP registrations. It said count does not matter and only the net effect is shown. It did not split SIP by ticket size or scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt AUM fall in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to institutional redemptions as corporates used liquidity for working capital during the war-related disruption, not to seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for alternates net yield and new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Net yield typically runs 90-100 bps depending on product mix. Life-cycle MF funds follow SEBI's predefined expense structure and start equity-heavy, then shift to debt nearer maturity.

qa_highlights.question: Is staff cost going to moderate after Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is the run rate. Compensation changes take effect from 1 April, with employee costs up 11% YoY. QoQ growth was partly due to reversals in Q4 FY26 and to campus hiring in Q1.

risks_watch: SIP trigger and June SIP run-rate (INR31,781 crore industry; company SIP+STP INR4,872 crore in June) as the next test of retail flow stickiness.
Debt AUM outflows from institutional and corporate liquidity; mix of debt AUM is a watch item.
MTM sensitivity: about 50% of the investment book is seed capital, so the other income line swings with markets (INR181 crore this quarter vs negative in Q4 FY26).
Alternates yield and mix shifts; PMS/AIF net yield of 95 bps with fees and commissions rising in line with volumes.

The moderator stated upfront that company financial performance, outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed. The CEO Baskar Subramanian framed AI as reshaping the video value chain across production, preparation (metadata, encoding, scheduling), distribution (agent-to-agent deals) and consumer discovery. He cited a claim that every $1 spent on technology brings $2 to $4 of human toil, and said most customers view AI as expansionary rather than a cost-saving tool today. No Q1 FY27 results, segment data or guidance were given.
guidance_outlook: No company guidance given; the moderator stated financial performance, business outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed.
Management described AI-driven production cost deflation as a multi-year shift, saying the next few years would bring a fundamental change, without quantifying it.
Management said outcome-based pricing is early and not yet visible in media, and that the core system is expected to stay as is while expansion revenue is driven by outcomes.
capex_capacity: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPUs and servers, and expects more progression in that direction; no Amagi capex or capacity figures were given.
Management said GPU costs are significant for video AI but did not quantify them; token cost is a small part of AI cost in video.
demand_pricing: Management says most customers are pursuing expansion (more channels, revenue opportunities) rather than AI cost savings today, citing Jevons' paradox.
Outcome-based pricing (per transaction, per result, per success) is being discussed in some markets, but management says it is not yet visible in media.

Management says token cost is a small part of AI cost in video; GPU costs are significant. It also cited an example of a scheduler's work falling from 8 hours to about 10 minutes of review under an agentic system.
Management described the metadata and preparation workload as a headcount constraint, with media companies creating about 6 hours of unique news daily and running content across 40-plus countries.

qa_highlights.question: What safeguards exist against hallucination and unpredictability given strict 99.9999% SLAs with clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the approach is to bring determinism to a non-deterministic problem through guardrails and engineered systems, noting that getting AI from demos to production is the hard part.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI improving prep-work speed and reducing pricing through deflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI mainly reduces human cost in preparation (e.g., speech-to-text making subtitling unnecessary) and expands what can be done rather than directly reducing price.

qa_highlights.question: Can AI move production and pre-production workflows to the cloud?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPU and server capacity, and expects more of this shift.

qa_highlights.question: Are there real-life examples of cost reduction or higher OTT/cable content from AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adoption is early, with some creators using AI for VFX and background creation, and microdrama as the most active area.

qa_highlights.question: Is there evidence of cost savings, given higher token costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said token cost is small relative to video GPU and human costs, and most customers are using AI for expansion, with cost savings secondary.

qa_highlights.question: Do agent-to-agent communications create network effects and first-mover advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said connecting two or more ecosystem parties through agentic infrastructure has high network-effect value, but the space is very early and standards are still forming.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI deepen client engagement and threaten horizontal SaaS or hyperscalers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued that vertical, mission-critical media software has a moat in enterprise context, which it sees as more durable than generic reasoning models.

qa_highlights.question: Will agentic AI materially cut customer operating costs and create pricing pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-job costs may deflate, but the volume of work customers want to do is expanding, which it characterised as a Jevons' paradox effect.

qa_highlights.question: How will vendor-client commercial models change as agentic AI spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outcome-driven pricing is being explored in other industries, but it is early and not yet prominent in media.

Rising GPU and infrastructure costs for video AI, which management said are material but did not quantify.

544698|2026-03.headline: H2 FY26 total income rose 28% YoY to INR12,656.59 lakh and net profit rose 158% to INR432.20 lakh; FY26 PAT was INR750.29 lakh.
544698|2026-03.overview: PAN HR Solution's first earnings call, held 12 June 2026 after its February 2026 BSE SME listing, covered H2 and full-year FY26 results. Management reported H2 total income of INR12,656.59 lakh (+28% YoY) and H2 net profit of INR432.20 lakh (+158% YoY), against a prior-year H2 that was smaller. Full-year PAT of INR750.29 lakh looked moderate because FY25 included a one-time INR6.5 crore prior-period income. The company ended FY26 with net worth of INR3,751 lakh, cash of INR2,434 lakh and no debt, and set out a plan to reach INR1,000 crore revenue by FY29.

financial_highlights.change: Full-year YoY comparison not stated; FY25 base included INR6.5 crore one-time exceptional prior-period income

segments.name: Manpower outsourcing / workforce deployment
segments.commentary: Deployed workforce grew from about 10,000 at IPO to over 11,000 on payroll as of the call. Clients are concentrated in e-commerce, quick commerce, logistics, warehousing and manufacturing; management cited more than 17 clients.

segments.name: Emerging services (3PL, payroll, compliance, HR outsourcing, white-collar hiring)
segments.commentary: Management said these are new or being scaled: 3PL and B2B models were not previously done, and white-collar one-time staffing has started. No revenue figures were given for these lines.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow FY27 turnover by approximately 40%.
Target revenue of INR1,000 crore by FY29 (within three years), with the 3PL model named as the first growth lever.
Priorities for FY27: deploy IPO proceeds into working capital, move toward pay-and-collect contracts, expand into new geographies and sectors, and grow payroll, compliance and HR services.
Management expects a higher-margin mix over time, but said some contracts carry lower margins while creating operating leverage.
capex_capacity: Workforce deployment rose from about 10,000 at IPO to more than 11,000 on payroll; the company said it now operates in the South and West as well as North and East.
Management said internal infrastructure is underused and that new services can run on existing infrastructure without major new investment.
IPO proceeds are to go mainly to working capital expansion, and acquisitions are under consideration; no specific acquisition target or deal size was named.
demand_pricing: Revenue in FY26 was affected by contract repricing and billing-cycle changes, as stated by management.

Management said it had turned away pay-and-collect clients in the prior year because of fund constraints and can now pursue them; pay-and-collect has started at one or two locations with existing clients.
Competitive positioning rests on compliance credibility (operating since 2015), balance-sheet strength, and an integrated single-window model covering salary, compliance and workforce management.
Management did not quantify pricing or margin changes.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors read moderate full-year growth versus strong H2 numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 shows strong growth; the full-year PAT gap reflects a FY25 base that included INR6.5 crore one-time prior-period income. It attributed the revenue slowdown to not taking pay-and-collect clients in FY25 for lack of funds.

qa_highlights.question: How will the IPO capital be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: First priority is business expansion and working capital; the company is also watching acquisition opportunities. No amount or timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the acquisition targets and why acquire?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets are workforce management, staffing and payroll companies with strong client bases; the rationale is to gain client databases and avoid duplicating infrastructure. No named targets or valuation were disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the INR1,000 crore FY29 revenue goal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the 3PL business with existing clients (not previously pursued due to funds), new areas, stronger existing-client relationships and acquisitions, targeting completion within three years.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins come under pressure with growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some contracts carry lower margins but generate operating leverage; the focus is on profitable growth and improving return ratios.

qa_highlights.question: What are the return-ratio expectations (ROE, ROCE)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said return ratios are a priority; temporary dips are possible while capital is deployed for growth. No ROE or ROCE figures were given.

risks_watch: Full-year PAT comparison is distorted by the FY25 one-time INR6.5 crore income; the underlying base needs confirming.
Revenue was hit by contract repricing and billing-cycle changes in FY26; watch whether these persist in FY27.

The 40% FY27 turnover target and INR1,000 crore FY29 goal depend on working-capital deployment, pay-and-collect contracts (which raise working-capital needs) and acquisitions with no named targets yet.
Margin dilution from lower-margin contracts and the new 3PL, white-collar and pay-and-collect mix.
Client concentration: management cited more than 17 clients, which is a small base for the stated scale-up.
The company said it has no debt, but no quarterly or segment breakdown was given.
544698|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and the balance sheet, but vague on specifics: acquisition targets, segment revenue, margins and return ratios were given only in general terms. Answers on the FY26 full-year profit gap were more defensive, and several answers repeated the strategy without numbers.
key_quotes: Our H2 revenue for FY 2025 increased from INR98.85 crores to INR126.57 crores this year, which shows a 28% year-on-year growth.
Investors should look at financial year 2026 as a stronger and clearer reflection of the company's actual business performance and earnings quality.
The target we have set for this year is to increase our turnover by approximately 40%.
Today we are a debt-free company, we don't have any liability, nor was there any before, and even now we don't have any liability.

544699|2026-06.headline: Aye Finance Q1 FY27: AUM up 28% YoY to INR7,324 crores, PAT up 144% to INR75 crores, credit cost eased to 4.01%.
544699|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 22% YoY to INR1,219 crores, the strongest first quarter on record, and AUM grew 28% YoY to INR7,324 crores. Gross NPA fell 28 bps QoQ to 4.49% and credit cost fell 29 bps QoQ to 4.01%, which management says is already at the top of the 3.5%-4% guidance band. Net total income rose 38% YoY to INR322 crores and NIM improved 20 bps QoQ to 15.9%. Fee income dropped QoQ on lower direct assignment volumes and a one-off FX gain last quarter, and management kept the FY27 guidance unchanged while signalling possible refinement at H1.

segments.name: Hypothecation loans
segments.commentary: Core product, ~24-month tenor, average ticket ~INR1.5 lakh, ~78% of portfolio; portfolio ROI ~27.5%-28%; PAR X ~7.5%, PAR 30 ~6.6%, PAR 90 ~5.35%.

segments.name: Mortgage / Micro LAP
segments.commentary: ~22% of portfolio; portfolio ROI ~23.5%; PAR X ~5%, PAR 30 ~5%, PAR 90 ~3%; LTV ~35%-40%. Management expects only marginal mix increase in FY27, with a longer-term target of ~30%-35%.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 25%-30% for FY27; Q1 AUM growth was 28% YoY.
Credit cost guided at 3.5%-4% for FY27; management says Q1 at top of band and expects improvement, with narrower guidance possible by end of H1. Long term, ~3%-3.5% once mortgage share reaches ~30%.
NIM guided flat at 14.25%-14.75%, with management flagging possible upside given Q1 NIM of 15.9%.
Opex-to-assets guided at 8.25%-8.75%; Q1 at 8.9%, with Q1-Q2 likely above band and Q3-Q4 expected inside it.

Borrowing cost expected to fall a further 10-15 bps after the India Ratings upgrade (IND A to A+, stable; CP to IND A1+). Lower cost on incremental borrowings is 20-25 bps over the year per the earlier statement.
Plan to add ~40-50 branches in FY27 (~10% of branch base, counting large branches). Team to grow ~10%. Medium-term opex target of 7%-7.5% over 3 years.

Medium term: vision of INR24,000 crores AUM within 5 years (~27%-28% CAGR). Product mix target over 3 years: 60%-70% hypothecation, ~30% Micro LAP, ~10% other secured products such as gold loans and solar loans.
Leverage at 3.15x; fresh equity needed at 4x-4.5x, which management says gives 2-2.5 years of growth runway (book to ~INR14,000 crores). Targeted ROA 4.5%-5% post-tax at 3.5%-4% credit cost.
capex_capacity: 571 branches across 18 states and 3 union territories as of June 2026; plan to add ~40-50 branches in FY27, with additions and splits visible between Q2 and Q3.
Branch strategy: ~10% annual growth in large-branch equivalents plus splits of mature branches (~44 splits last year, reported profitable from day one).
Team growth ~10% (13%-15% manpower increase mentioned for new branches), against a base of ~11,000 employees.
AUM per employee up 12% YoY.
demand_pricing: Credit policy tightened: approval share fell from ~55% to ~45% of logged cases, while customer additions still rose 38% YoY.

Management says the micro-enterprise market is under-penetrated (Aye has penetrated ~2%-3% of it); digital fintech and UPI lenders are seen as a limited overlap, with 7%-8% of fresh sourcing from digital channels.
Seasonality: Q1 typically ~20%-22% of annual disbursements; H1 ~40%, H2 ~60%. April was seasonally weak but May-June collection efficiency was ~99.3%.
Non-OD collection efficiency 99.2%; Bucket 1 collection 54.5%. Post-PAR 90 collection ~29%-30%, per management.
Pre-closure rate ~3%-3.5% annualised for hypothecation and ~5%-5.5% blended. Direct assignment target kept at 5%-7% of AUM (about 5% today).

financial_highlights.change: +28% YoY, +4% QoQ from INR7,044 crores in March 2026
-28 bps QoQ from 4.77%; vs 4.6% a year ago
-29 bps QoQ; includes ~INR6 crores management overlay
vs 9.5% at end of FY26; guidance 8.25%-8.75%
DA income ~INR20 crores absent; ~INR12 crores FX gain moved to OCI

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 3.5%-4% credit cost guidance well above peers despite tighter underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hypothecation (~24-month tenor, ~INR1.5 lakh ticket) differs from peers' Micro LAP book; terminal losses are ~5.5%-6% for both products, translating to ~3.5% annual credit cost, with ~3% possible in a good year. Q1 is already at the top of the band; guidance could narrow by end-H1.

qa_highlights.question: Fee and other income fell QoQ: what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed ~INR32-33 crores of decline to no direct assignment in Q1 (DA ~INR20 crores last quarter) and ~INR12 crores FX gain last quarter now moved to OCI, plus lower cross-sell on lower disbursements. Cross-sell insurance income was INR9 crores in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Can NIM exceed the upper end of 14.25%-14.75% guidance, and how do yield and cost of funds move?
qa_highlights.answer: Weighted cost of borrowing fell to 10.78% from 10.87%; incremental borrowing cost ~10.20%, ~60 bps lower. Further 10-15 bps drop expected from the India Ratings upgrade. Portfolio yield 22.4% expected to drift slightly lower as mortgage grows, but NIM guidance held flat.

qa_highlights.question: How much management overlay is in the credit cost and on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Around INR6 crores of overlay was created within the Q1 4.01% credit cost; total overlay on balance sheet is INR11 crores, in Stage 2 and Stage 3. Target overlay is about 0.5% of book, used to smooth cross-cycle credit cost within 3.5%-4%.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term: how achievable is INR24,000 crores AUM in 5 years, and what is the product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 2%-3% market penetration and branch-led origination; target mix over 3 years is 60%-70% hypothecation, ~30% Micro LAP and ~10% other secured products such as gold and solar loans. About 55,000 declined customers are seen seeking gold loans, with 20%-plus doing so.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAR X at ~7% be sufficient to deliver the 3.5%-4% credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes: at ~7% PAR X, credit cost of 3.5%-4% and post-tax ROA of 4.5%-5% are achievable. Management also guided sustainable PAR X at about 6%-6.5% and expects Q3-Q4 PAR to moderate from 7.01%.

risks_watch: Opex-to-assets at 8.9% in Q1 is above the 8.25%-8.75% guidance band; management expects Q1-Q2 above band and Q3-Q4 inside it.
PAR X at 7.01% and PAR 90 for mortgage (~3%) vs hypothecation (~5.35%); management has limited deep-bucket collection capacity in mortgage and says improvement depends on it.
Monsoon below normal (IMD ~92% of LPA) with stress possible in central India and southern peninsula; management says large states are not expected to be affected.
Credit cost guidance and NIM guidance may be refined at end-H1; management flagged possible upside on both.
Fee income is lower with no DA in Q1; DA target kept at 5%-7% of AUM, currently about 5%.
Q1 disbursements are seasonal (about 20%-22% of annual); Q2 and Q3 branch additions are back-loaded and the 40-50 branch plan needs to show up in those quarters.
Capital adequacy and leverage: leverage 3.15x, with fresh equity needed at 4x-4.5x (about 2-2.5 years of runway); ROE currently low due to IPO capital.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 has definitely been encouraging where we are already at the top of that band that we are talking of, and as we move into the subsequent quarters, we do feel that this number should improve further.

So, answer to your question is that yes, 7% is good enough. It will deliver to us the credit cost that we're talking of, 3.5% to 4%, and it will deliver the ROA which we are targeting, which is probably 4.5% to 5%.
So, I think right now, 8.9% versus the highest 8.75%, I think we are very much there.
We are targeting an AUM growth, as we had said in the guidance, between 25% to 30% for this year.
544699|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, asset quality and funding, with management stating that Q1 credit cost and opex are already close to guided bands. Cautious on exact guidance: refinement is deferred to end-H1, and management declined to quantify slippage and deeper-bucket recovery.

544699|2026-09.headline: Aye Finance Q2 FY27: PAT more than doubled to INR87 crore (+151% YoY) as credit cost fell to 3.82% and NIM hit 15.6%, above the 14.25-14.75% guidance.
544699|2026-09.overview: AUM rose 26% YoY to INR7,597 crore (+4% QoQ) and Q2 disbursements were INR1,403 crore (+10% YoY, +15% QoQ), with repeat loans down 3% YoY. Credit cost fell for a seventh straight quarter to 3.82%, now inside the 3.5-4% guidance, and GNPA eased to 4.20%. Opex ratio fell to 8.6% from 8.9% QoQ, and management says NIM is running ahead of guidance partly because a rating upgrade to IND A+ was not factored in. Management reiterated FY27 guidance and flagged that the second half, which carries about 60% of disbursements, is where delivery will be tested.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR65 crore in H1 FY26 (+148%)

segments.name: Hypothecation loans (core)
segments.commentary: Management describes itself as the dominant player with no meaningful competition in this segment. Productivity per loan officer reached 4.85 files per month in Q2, against about 4.2 in FY26 and a FY27 budget of about 5.

segments.name: Micro-LAP / mortgage
segments.commentary: Mortgage PAR X rose about 1 percentage point over the last quarter to around 6%, still below hypothecation. Management tightened policy and disbursements are being slowed, mainly in parts of MP and Gujarat. Mortgage foreclosures are rising to about 22-23% of the portfolio.

segments.name: Cattle / dairy
segments.commentary: Cattle book is held at roughly 25-28% of AUM, underwritten with a minimum of four to six high-yielding cattle, and static-pool data is described as marginally better than the market. Management does not plan to grow it aggressively.

segments.name: Gold loans (planned)
segments.commentary: Under evaluation as a pilot, with new branch setups in cities where existing branches sit. Around 20% of micro-enterprise customers already hold gold loans. Management expects to update on the plan later in the year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 25-30% reiterated; management says it is in the range and 30% is possible but not committed. Three-year vision of 28-33% AUM CAGR and 4-4.5% ROA was shared in July.
FY27 credit cost guided at 3.5-4%, with management expecting to average around 3.5% plus or minus a few bps and exit the year lower.
NIM guidance of 14.25-14.75% maintained for now; management may revisit it in Q3 if the upside persists.
FY27 opex ratio guided at 8.25-8.75%; management expects it to move into range in H2 and to be around 8.5% for FY27.
FY27 ROA guided at 4-4.5%, with ROA expected to move into range as H2 volumes build.

Next year (FY28) levers cited: about 50 bps opex-ratio benefit, 10-25 bps lower credit cost, and about 25 bps lower interest cost, with ROA guidance said to be unaffected by insurance commission changes.
PAR X targeted below 7% by H1 and below 6.5% by year-end. Non-OD collection efficiency expected in the 99.2-99.3% range.
No fresh equity needed for about 2 years at current capital; management sees leverage moving to 4-4.5x, implying ROE in the high teens to low 20s over time.
capex_capacity: Branches held at 571 at the end of H1 FY27. More than 30 new branches are to become operational in Q3 FY27, and about 80 branches (35-40 new plus about 40 splits) are planned for the year.
Existing branch infrastructure is said to support about INR4,000-4,500 crore of additional AUM over the near term.
AUM per branch was INR13.3 crore in Q2 (INR12.8 crore in Q1). AUM per employee was INR0.67 crore vs INR0.57 crore a year ago.
Employee count budgeted to grow 12-15% in FY27. Headcount is expected to rise 5-7% in H2, mostly in Q3, for distribution and collections.
Pilot gold loan branches are planned for this year and are not expected to strain the opex budget.
demand_pricing: Repeat loans fell 3% YoY in Q2 (up 10% QoQ). Management attributes this to festive timing shifting into Q3 and expects a stronger Q3.
Management says it is not using average ticket size to grow the book; growth is coming from productivity.

Drought has been declared in parts of Maharashtra, Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh, which account for about 18% of AUM. Disbursements are being consciously slowed there, with branch-level calls in MP and Gujarat.

Bucket 1 collection efficiency was 52.8%, dipping over the last three to four months (UP included). Management attributes this to pre-festive cash-flow tightness and expects improvement after November.
Non-OD collection efficiency was 99.2%. Bihar, UP and Rajasthan, the largest states, were largely unaffected by the monsoon.
Borrowing rose to about INR1,100 crore in Q1 and about INR1,200 crore in Q2. The bank share of borrowings rose to 35% from 32%, with no tightening seen from banks.
About 8-9% of primary borrowers overlap with MFI loans (about 30-32% at household level), and FOIR includes MFI obligations.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of reaching the top end of FY27 AUM growth (30%) given the H2 weighting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the H2 is about 60% of disbursements and that it is in the 25-30% range. Reaching the higher end is possible, depending on H2 execution, with repeat loans, gold loans and new branches as levers.

qa_highlights.question: Target ROE and dilution risk over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA of about 4.5% combined with 4-4.5x leverage implies ROE in the high teens to low 20s, built up gradually as debt is added. Management does not expect dilution over the next two financial years, given net worth of about INR2,600 crore plus.

qa_highlights.question: Asset quality and credit cost outlook for H2, and cattle portfolio behaviour in inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost is expected to fall toward 3.5% with a lower exit rate. Cattle underwriting requires four to six high-yielding cattle and avoids marginal dairy farmers; static-pool data is marginally better than peers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ECL provisions change, and what was the write-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management overlays were added to Stage 2 and Stage 3 this quarter (Stage 2 moved from INR42 crore to INR48 crore). Write-offs rose modestly to about INR95 crore, including about INR45 crore already fully provided, so credit cost was flat.

qa_highlights.question: Fundraising conditions given rising rates and liquidity tightening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reported no difficulty. Borrowings were about INR1,100 crore in Q1 and about INR1,200 crore in Q2, the bank share rose to 35%, and the incremental cost was 10.04%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the insurance commission impact can be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 50 bps of opex-ratio benefit, 25 bps of lower interest cost even after a 25 bps rate rise, and 10-25 bps of lower credit cost next year, which together should absorb the impact without repricing. A 50 bps rate hike is estimated at 7 bps ROA impact in FY27 and 15 bps in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NIM guidance kept at 14.25-14.75% when Q2 is 15.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited expected yield pressure from the growing ML book and slow repeat business, plus higher borrowing costs. It will revisit guidance in Q3 if the upside holds.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company insured against drought or natural catastrophe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said insuring the full book would not be ROA-accretive given low loss rates. CGFMU cover is used selectively, at about INR200-300 crore of the book. Credit life insurance would not help in a drought.

risks_watch: H2 execution: about 60% of disbursements fall in H2, and management says the top end of the 25-30% AUM growth guidance depends on how H2 plays out. Repeat loans (down 3% YoY in Q2) and new branches (30+ operational in Q3) are the levers.

Asset quality: Bucket 1 collection efficiency fell to 52.8% over the last three to four months, with UP included; management expects improvement after November. Watch whether PAR X falls below 7% by H1 and below 6.5% by year-end.

Drought exposure: Maharashtra, Karnataka and MP (about 18% of AUM) are under drought declarations; disbursements are slowed there and micro-LAP is tightened in parts of MP and Gujarat. Mortgage PAR X rose about 1 percentage point in a quarter to around 6%.

Insurance commission regulation: management says ROA guidance is unchanged even with potential changes, offset by about 50 bps opex-ratio benefit, 25 bps interest cost benefit and 10-25 bps lower credit cost. Actual regulatory outcome is still open.
NIM: Q2 NIM of 15.6% is above the 14.25-14.75% guidance, which is kept for now due to expected yield pressure from the ML book, slow repeat business and rate hikes. Management will revisit in Q3.
Gold loan pilot: planned new branch setups in existing cities; management expects to update later in the year. Watch opex impact and any rollout scale.
Funding: bank share of borrowings rose to 35% from 32%, and incremental cost is 10.04%. Watch for any tightening as rates rise.
key_quotes: So, this solid first half has significantly enhanced our conviction to deliver on our stated FY27 guidance.
Whether we will be in the closer to 30%, I wouldn't like to commit now. But is it possible? Yes, it is definitely on our hindsight.
The primary reason is that our guidance had factored in more aggressive increase in repo rates.
I think our guidance for ROA should stay untouched.
544699|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on headline numbers (NIM, credit cost, PAT) and on FY27 guidance, though the CEO declined to commit to the top end of AUM growth and deferred the NIM guidance revision to Q3. Management was more cautious on the near-term collection trend, attributing the Bucket 1 dip to pre-festive cash-flow tightness rather than a structural cause.

544700|2026-06.headline: Fractal Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR 912.5 crore (9% constant currency), with TMT down 22% weighing on growth.
544700|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 20% YoY and 3% QoQ to INR 912.5 crore, but constant-currency growth was 9% and TMT (down 22%) was the drag; management says growth ex-TMT was 37%. Profitability improved: adjusted EBITDA margin rose 189 bps YoY to 16.8%, and net income grew 92% to INR 72 crore (7.9% margin). Management said TMT bottomed and expects sequential growth next quarter, and CFO Ashwath Bhat announced this is his last call. Q1 included a one-month impact of a merit increase effective June 1, with about 120-130 bps full P&L impact expected in Q2.

segments.name: Healthcare and Life Sciences (vertical)
segments.commentary: Grew 69% YoY and is now the second-largest vertical; management noted growth was lower than the previous quarter's reported rate.

segments.name: Banking and Financial Services (vertical)
segments.commentary: Grew 36% YoY; new BFSI chief practice officer appointed.

segments.name: CPG and Retail (vertical)
segments.commentary: Largest vertical, grew 19% YoY.

segments.name: TMT (vertical)
segments.commentary: Declined 22% YoY and was the main drag; management expects healthy sequential growth next quarter, driven by new deals from existing clients.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Europe grew 25% and Americas 24% YoY; APAC and others fell 2%, attributed to TMT and the Middle East conflict.

segments.name: Fractal Alpha (Asper.ai and Analytics Vidhya)
segments.commentary: Like-for-like revenue grew 20% YoY; Analytics Vidhya grew 57% (42% in USD), Asper flat. Gross margin 65%; segment loss INR 14 crore vs INR 4 crore a year ago, due to moving iqigai and EdTech teams from Fractal.ai. Asper ARR up 59% YoY in USD to $9 million.

segments.name: Qure.ai (associate)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 160% YoY to INR 24 crore; share of loss INR 23 crore vs INR 22 crore; backlog above INR 100 crore vs around INR 20 crore a year ago.

segments.name: Cogentiq
segments.commentary: More than 10 early clients across industries; product license revenue about 3% of total revenue; Cogentiq revenue not separately reported yet.

guidance_outlook: TMT expected to show healthy sequential growth in Q2 FY27 and thereafter, based on existing deal pipeline.
Management expects overall growth to improve once TMT stabilises; no numeric FY27 guidance given.
Merit increase effective June 1: about 75 bps gross margin and 120-130 bps full P&L impact in Q1; three months of impact in Q2.
R&D to rise toward 10% of revenue, funded only from expanded gross margins.
Output/outcome/license revenue mix at 42%; target 60% over the next few quarters.
Asper revenue expected to be much stronger in H2 FY27 as signed ARR converts to revenue.
capex_capacity: R&D spend INR 61 crore in Q1 (+31% YoY), with focus on Cogentiq, Asper and Analytics Vidhya.
Management plans to raise R&D to as much as 10% of revenue, gated by gross margin expansion.
New go-to-market structure under a Chief Commercial Officer, with AIT, AIF and AIW vectors; new leaders hired for verticals and Europe.
Cogentiq product build-outs in underwriting, e-commerce, supply chain and customer service; product leaders being hired.
demand_pricing: Largest current deal: a single large healthcare AI foundations and data modernisation program won in Q1; details to be shared within days.
Larger RFPs are emerging with bigger deal sizes; management expects these to show in numbers over the next few years.
Competition is intensifying as many players target AI-led work.
TMT weakness attributed partly to large tech firms shifting spend from opex to AI capex; management said it takes most of the blame on execution.
Five of the largest deals in Q1 came through partners (Databricks, OpenAI, Anthropic); partner-led revenue is small and not yet reported; 42 TTM joint engagements cited.
Client count: 5 clients above INR 20 million TTM (from 4), 19 above INR 5 million (from 18), 58 above INR 1 million (from 54).

qa_highlights.question: What supports the expected sequential TMT recovery, and is the Cogentiq deal flow product-led or services-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Recovery comes from new deals with existing clients, not new logos. Cogentiq deals are described as mostly product-led, with some FDE or implementation component.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any client-specific issue in TMT, and when was the FY27 wage increase effective?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will stop discussing client-specific issues unless dramatic. TMT was worse than expected. The merit increase was effective June 1, instead of the usual April 1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HLS growth slow, and how will FY27 growth trend across verticals?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-TMT growth is 35-37%; total growth is about 20% because of TMT. Growth is expected across verticals, with new leaders being hired for Europe and BFSI.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Fractal Alpha losses rise, and what drives the Qure.ai outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Alpha loss rose to INR 14 crore from INR 4 crore due to investment in Analytics Vidhya after moving iqigai and EdTech teams. Asper flat in Q1 but ARR up 59%, so H2 expected stronger. Qure.ai revenue up 160% with backlog above INR 100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Cogentiq revenue contribution and the R&D and mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: License revenue is about 3% of revenue and is expected to rise. Cogentiq revenue will be reported from next quarter. Outcome/output/license mix is 42%, targeting 60%. R&D may rise toward 10% of revenue only with margin expansion.

544709|2026-06.headline: Gaudium IVF Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.1% YoY to ₹19.4 crore, while reported EBITDA margin fell to 12.5% from 29% on expansion and marketing costs.
544709|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 9.1% YoY to ₹19.4 crore against ₹17.8 crore in Q1 FY26, with management attributing the slow growth to seasonality and pre-launch work. Reported EBITDA fell 52.96% to ₹2.4 crore and PAT from continuing operations fell 42.27% to ₹1.8 crore, which management tied to front-loaded expansion costs and a one-time pan-India marketing push for the SiD and ERICA AI embryology tools. The South Extension (New Delhi) hub became operational on 16 July 2026, with Gurgaon and Nagpur guided to open in about 10 and 25 days. Management reiterated FY27 targets of about 30% revenue growth and 10 new hubs, but the quarter's growth rate is far below that target.

segments.name: IVF (core)
segments.commentary: Anchors the business; management says the Janakpuri (Delhi) flagship is growing about 30% YoY. Pharmacy and hospital services are described as lower-margin and complementary, with no separate figures disclosed.

segments.name: Pharmacy and hospital services
segments.commentary: Supply fertility medications and allied women's health services (gynaecology, obstetrics, minimally invasive procedures). No revenue or margin split given on the call.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of about 30% revenue growth for FY27 by year-end, after an analyst challenged whether 40%+ was achievable; it said the growth rate would pick up over Q2 and Q4.
Adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to return to FY26 levels by year-end, per management's answer to a direct question.
Target of 10 new hubs in FY27, then 8 in FY28 and 1 in FY29; South Extension is the first of the 19-centre IPO-funded expansion.
Breakeven for new hubs is said to come in about three months historically, against a six-month industry-type benchmark.
Lucknow Women Hospital project of up to ₹15 crore, funded from internal accruals, with commercialisation expected in FY28-FY29.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex of about ₹25 crore for 10 new hubs at about ₹2.5 crore per hub (₹1 crore construction, ₹1.5 crore lab machinery), funded from IPO proceeds and internal accruals; described as on track.
South Extension, New Delhi hub operational 16 July 2026, with the Gaudium Signature Lab (AI embryology).
Gurgaon hub expected to be operational about 10 days after the call; Nagpur (Tier 2) about 25 days after the call.
Patna centre relocated to Kankarbagh medical hub and became operational about three days before the call.
Mature hub volume benchmarks: about 30 cycles a year for a Tier 2 hub and about 50 for a metro hub.
demand_pricing: Q1 is seasonally weak (heat) and Q3 is weak (festivals); management said Q2 and Q4 make up for it, and that historically growth has been about 30% YoY against an industry CAGR of 10-12%.
Initial IVF package starts at about ₹2 lakh per patient and can go up to ₹20 lakh for complex cases; per-cycle cost cited as about ₹2 lakh.
International patients are about 25-30% of the patient mix; three international spokes have begun in Paris, Nigeria and Sydney.

Management says the organised segment is about 30% of the market versus 70% unorganised, and expects consolidation as the ART Act is implemented; it also said full implementation may take about another year.
HDFC Bank patient financing tie-up is aimed at Tier 2 and Tier 3 patients.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 growth only 9%, and is 30-40% FY27 growth and FY26-level margins achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q1 seasonality and build-up work on centres under construction; it said South Extension is already contributing and reiterated 30% growth and FY26-level adjusted margins by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly does a new hub break even, and at what scale is it profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said breakeven historically comes in about three months, and its centres have broken even within that period wherever they have opened.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter hospital business in Lucknow, and is it funded from IPO proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Lucknow was already on the IVF expansion list, that the women's hospital is a step toward women's health beyond IVF, and that it is funded from internal accruals, not IPO money.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unit economics per hub (capex, package size, cycles)?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex averages ₹2.5 crore per centre; initial package ₹2 lakh up to ₹20 lakh; mature Tier 2 hubs target about 30 cycles a year and metro hubs about 50.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin decline from a one-off expense?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin decline mainly to a one-time pan-India marketing push for SiD and ERICA, expected to pay off over the rest of the year.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue growth be split into patient volume and revenue per patient?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a volume versus price split; it repeated the seasonality explanation and did not address the service-mix question directly.

qa_highlights.question: How are the AI tools differentiated and what is the benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SiD (sperm selection) and ERICA (embryo assessment) are the first such tools in India, certified by IVF 2.0, and show early results of about 8% higher first-attempt success; these are early results and not yet validated over a longer period.

EBITDA margin of 12.5% versus the guided return to FY26 levels; management calls the drag one-off, but it needs verification next quarter.
Early AI-tool success-rate data (about 8% improvement) is not yet validated over a longer period; management said this would need time.
Competitive intensity and the pace of ART Act implementation across states, which management said could take about another year.
Execution on hub openings (Gurgaon, Nagpur) and on the balance of the 10 FY27 hubs; the Lucknow hospital adds a new business line and capex of up to ₹15 crore.

544710|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue fell to about INR70.6 crore on customer-side delays, while H2 EBITDA margin rose to 11.77% and PAT reached INR3.25 crore.
544710|2026-03.overview: Management attributed the year-on-year revenue decline to customer site delays rather than weak demand, with roughly INR31 crore of transformer orders and INR3 crore of another order deferred from March 2026 into FY27. FY26 total income was INR70.60 crore, EBITDA INR7.31 crore (10.39% margin) and PAT INR4.50 crore. H2 FY26 total income was INR42.59 crore, EBITDA INR5.01 crore (11.77%) and PAT INR3.25 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue of INR120-180 crore, an EBITDA margin of 13-15% and a PAT margin of 9-11%, and said no dividend is expected for now.

Management cited FY24 margin near 5% and FY25 near 11% (analyst framing)

segments.commentary: About INR8 crore of FY26 revenue, roughly 10%. Management said package and compact substations together make up about 90% of the product mix.

segments.commentary: Management said about INR31 crore of FY26 business came from the BESS-related segment. No BESS entry is planned, and the EV charging-station electrification role is a future opportunity, not yet booked.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR120-180 crore, with the deferred orders expected to be recognised in the current year.
Revenue growth guided at 60-80% for the next year, and 30-50% thereafter.
EBITDA margin target of 13-15% and PAT margin target of 9-11%, with about 10% as an average.
No dividend for now. Board may consider a dividend policy in 1-2 years, given working capital and capex needs.
Existing plant can handle about INR150 crore of business and up to INR200 crore if deliveries run smoothly.
Management expects to use about 90% of capacity in FY27 and says current capacity is at 75-80% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue from operations decline in FY26 vs FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said revenue fell about INR9 crore because customer EPC projects were delayed. About INR31 crore of transformers (35 units, about 25 made, worth INR21-22 crore) and INR3 crore were deferred to FY27 after a Maharashtra government dispute and site delays.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend policy and when will capital be returned?
qa_highlights.answer: No dividend is expected because the company is in an expansion phase with heavy working capital needs for the INR156 crore order book. The Board may consider a policy in 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company entering BESS or energy storage?
qa_highlights.answer: Not currently. Management said BESS makers are existing clients, and entering that segment could cost those orders. Focus is on high-capacity, high-voltage transformers.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue growth and PAT guidance applies going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided FY27 revenue of INR120-180 crore, growth of 60-80% next year and 30-50% thereafter. EBITDA margin target is 13-15%, PAT margin 9-11%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company manage raw material price risk and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it keeps about 1-1.5 months of oil and accessories in stock, books copper and CRGO for about 1 month, and hedges about 15% for up to 3 months. Orders with delivery beyond 3 months carry IEEMA price variation clauses.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Russia MOU and the EV charging project worth?

The NHEV project's CSS scope is about INR1,600 crore over 3-4 years on 450 stations, with an LOI issued and 10-15 stations expected by year-end.

544711|2026-03.headline: Kiaasa Retail FY26 revenue of ₹134.63 crore, EBITDA margin 17.8% and PAT ₹11.17 crore (+24% YoY); plan of 250 EBOs by 2028.
544711|2026-03.overview: Kiaasa Retail, a Tier 2/3-focused omni-channel women's ethnic wear brand listed on BSE SME in March 2026, reported FY26 revenue from operations of ₹134.63 crore, EBITDA of ₹24 crore (17.8% margin) and net profit of ₹11.17 crore (+24% YoY). Same-store sales growth accelerated to 12.89%, and the company had 124+ active EBOs across 70+ cities as of May 2026. Management attributed margin expansion to sourcing efficiencies and bulk procurement, and laid out a 250-store target by 2028 and 35% revenue CAGR ambition to FY30. Online contribution remains minimal at about 1-2% of revenue.

Management reiterated long-term vision: revenue CAGR of about 35% and EBITDA CAGR of about 45% through FY30; analyst summary was confirmed as 'yes, almost' with no formal EBITDA target given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 400-500 bps EBITDA margin expansion to 17-18%, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited improved sourcing efficiency, better vendor negotiation through bulk procurement and tighter control of operating parts; said cost minimisation will drive better margins over the next five years, without a quantified baseline.

qa_highlights.question: How is the shift to Tier 2/3 cities affecting store-level margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tier 2/3 cities now contribute the most, with consumers willing to pay for affordable luxury; ASP of ₹2,000-2,500 is an aggregate, and the plan is to build footfall first and then raise ASP with new items.

qa_highlights.question: How will the IPO proceeds (about ₹46 crore) be deployed and what revenue will follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Proceeds are for store opening only, covering capex and inventory, to open around 66 stores in the next two years; no revenue figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Store sizes, unit economics and capex for new stores; revenue and EBITDA targets for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Current stores are 700-1,000 sq ft; new stores to be around 1,500 sq ft in bigger cities, with some 1,200-1,500 sq ft formats. No EBITDA target given; referred to slide 20 for the FY30 vision of 35% revenue CAGR and EBITDA growth of roughly 45% CAGR.

qa_highlights.question: What share of same-store growth came from volume versus pricing, and why is ASP up while bill value is flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split volume and price. It cited brand awareness, repeat customers and new signature stories for ASP lift, and said store staff up-selling is lagging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MBO/LFS margin profile and working capital cycle, and what is the Nine99 payback?
qa_highlights.answer: MBO margin for partner is 28-32%, so PAT impact is limited but it adds footfall and awareness. Nine99 stores are cheap, low-rent, single-staff units; no payback period or revenue split was given.

qa_highlights.question: How does the FY30 revenue CAGR of 35% reconcile with FY26 growth of 11.2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan includes about 100 more stores beyond 250 by 2030, online growth, and 600-1,000 LFS counters by 2030.

qa_highlights.answer: Online is about 1-2% of revenue today and expected to reach about 10-12% over the next couple of years; no split for FY27 was given.

544717|2026-03.headline: CleanMax FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 28% to INR1,295 crore and PAT to INR86 crore; contracted capacity 5.7 GW with at least 1.5 GW addition guided for FY27.
544717|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue and EBITDA each grew about 28%, with EBITDA at INR1,295 crore against INR1,015 crore, and consolidated PAT rose to about INR86 crore from about INR19 crore. Operational capacity reached 3.1 GW after adding about 1,400 MW, and contracted capacity stood at 5.7 GW including 2.6 GW yet to be executed. Management guided to at least 1,500 MW of RE power sales additions in FY27 but gave no financial guidance. Key new risks raised were Rajasthan CTU curtailment (Bikaner 2 substation at about 30%) and the proposed deviation settlement mechanism (DSM) rules, which management has not yet quantified.

segments.name: RE Power Sales (C&I PPAs)
segments.commentary: Operational capacity 3.1 GW plus 2.6 GW contracted and under execution, total 5.7 GW; about 90% of EBITDA, with EBITDA margin 83.5% and gross margin around 92-93%. Average PPA tenor 23.17 years.

segments.name: RE Services (build-own-transfer style)
segments.commentary: Operational capacity 555 MW with another 215 MW under construction; EBITDA margin rose to 19.6% from 14.4%. Revenue growth about 28-30% across both segments.

guidance_outlook: Minimum 1,500 MW of RE Power Sales capacity addition in FY27; management said it is very confident of achieving this.
No financial guidance given; management reiterated reported EBITDA has historically been about 1.1x run-rate EBITDA, described as a past pattern rather than a forecast.
Storage/BESS response to DSM and curtailment to be announced in about three to four months.
Management expects EBITDA margin on RE Power Sales to reach nearly 86% in 3-4 years from about 83% today.
Grid forecast for end of Bikaner 2 backdown is September 2026, which management urged investors to treat conservatively.
Net debt to EBITDA target range of 5 to 5.5x; asset-level net debt to EBITDA cited at about 4.3x.

Contracted pipeline of 2.6 GW yet to be executed at start of FY27; management said 100% of capacity expected in FY27 is already contracted.
A 530 MW CTU project at Koppal in Karnataka (450 MW wind, 80 MW solar) is being added in FY27; a 525 MW CTU project in Rajasthan is about 13% of run-rate EBITDA.
Approximately 1 GW of the FY27 additions expected in STU projects.
Solar commissioning planned to be light in July-September 2026 quarter; module deliveries for solar to resume from September or October 2026.
Under construction in Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and Uttarakhand, adding new states; currently dispatching power in more than seven states.
demand_pricing: Data and AI customers are 42% of contracted capacity (about 2,400 MW), up from 14% (about 260 MW) on 1 April 2024; named clients include Princeton Digital Group, Iron Mountain, STT Data, and global big tech (Apple, Meta, Google, Amazon per management).
Repeat business was 74% of new volumes contracted in FY26; 82% of volumes are with AA/AAA or MNC clients, 96% with A-rated and above; 588 customers.
Contracted tariff on 2.6 GW under execution averages about INR3.85/unit (about 70% solar, 30% wind, negligible storage).
About 1,600-1,700 MW of the 5.7 GW is contract-for-difference (VPPA/I-REC type) with firm price exposure; management said there is no merchant price exposure on these.
Average PPA tenor 23.17 FY26 (22.73 FY25, 21.54 FY24); average lock-in about 18 years; no client disputes across more than 1,100 contracts.

Management expects module-cost increases from ALMM to pass through to tariffs; customer savings fall from about 30-35% to about 22-25%, with demand still robust; buying accelerated ahead of the June 2026 transition.
Reported grid uptime 99.24% in FY26; wind PLF rose from 32% to 35%, while solar PLF was slightly lower on weaker radiation.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Iran war and supply constraints on capex, module costs and interest rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not seen material adverse movement in equipment availability or capital costs attributable to the Iran war, while acknowledging a volatile situation.

qa_highlights.question: Share of under-construction CTU capacity, curtailment exposure and PPA protection?
qa_highlights.answer: The 530 MW Koppal CTU project is mostly wind in South India where curtailment is seen as minimal; PPAs give no protection if the grid curtails, since corporate customers do not pay for performance.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the new deviation settlement mechanism (DSM) on revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: No final decision and no internal impact estimate yet; the rules are sub-judice and the government is in talks. Storage is being evaluated to limit DSM downside, with an update in three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Nature of INR414 crore pre-tax cash flow hedge gain and negative minority interest?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedge is a balance-sheet fair-value entry on VPPA/I-REC contracts with zero P&L impact given fixed tariffs; minority interest is negative because young SPVs (asset age under two years) carry interest and depreciation before profits.

qa_highlights.question: BESS in the contracted portfolio and tariffs?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 5-7 MW of BESS within the 2,600 MW under execution; management would not separate tariffs for storage.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of rising module prices on IRRs?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariffs are expected to adjust to module costs; management said it prices to a constant target IRR, with no expected impact on margins or volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bidding pipeline and win rate, and are bids outside coal being pursued?

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT margin fall while EBITDA grew, and is the depreciation policy different?

544912|2026-06.headline: Prasol Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.7% YoY to INR433.6 crores and EBITDA to INR90.3 crores, helped by one-off inventory gains of about INR25 crores.

FY27 guidance of INR1,550-1,650 crores revenue and INR240-250 crores adjusted EBITDA excludes these gains, and management described a 15-16% year-end EBITDA margin. A Phase 1 capex of INR250-300 crores for existing products (about 60,000 tpa of added capacity) was outlined.
