544913|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to Rs.107 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to Rs.23 crore, with margin at 21.3% and a Rs.982 crore order book.
544913|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs.107 crore, up 36% YoY, led by domestic facade (Rs.62 crore, +93%) and fenestration (Rs.6 crore, +127%), while international fell 12% to Rs.39 crore on delivery timing. EBITDA grew 9% to Rs.23 crore, and margin fell to 21.3% because of lower international contribution and a shift to DDP freight billing at cost. Management attributed about 1.5 points of the margin gap to freight pass-through and said the underlying margin is in line with FY26. PAT of Rs.17 crore grew more slowly than EBITDA due to lower other income (prior-year property sale gain) and higher depreciation from new capacity. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 25% revenue growth, 23-25% EBITDA margin and 18-20% PAT margin, while flagging a weak first half and a heavier Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why has margin risen above pre-COVID levels on lower revenue?

qa_highlights.question: What is the glass processing unit timeline and benefit?

qa_highlights.question: What is the order-book and growth outlook?

qa_highlights.question: What are the market share and competitive position?

544914|2026-06.headline: Steamhouse Q1 FY27 PAT rose 80.25% YoY to INR18.34 crore on 16.7% steam volume growth; EBITDA margin 24.05%.
544914|2026-06.overview: Steamhouse reported record quarterly steam volumes of about 3,05,816 tons, up 16.7% YoY and 11.52% QoQ, with revenue from operations up 13.35% to INR128.62 crore. EBITDA rose 60.08% to INR30.93 crore, lifting margin to 24.05% (up 702 bps), while PAT rose 80.25% to INR18.34 crore. Management attributed the gains to higher volumes, utilisation (41.40% vs 36.06% YoY) and operating leverage, and noted the exit from low-margin coal trading. Gross debt rose to INR359.48 crore from INR281.62 crore at FY26 end, with IPO proceeds earmarked for debt reduction and capacity expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in the business across quarters, and what explains the Q1 volume jump over Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no real consumption seasonality, but monsoon is challenging (wet fuel, flooded industrial clusters). Q1 volume growth was attributed to chemical and pharma demand recovering and repeat customers.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the 345 TPH capacity is contracted, and can customers terminate contracts early?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of the 345 TPH installed capacity is tied up under contracts. Tenure ranges 1 to 10 years with non-exit clauses, and management said customers rarely move to captive boilers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value proposition to win customers from competitors or in-house boilers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is generally no competitor in most geographies. Claimed cost saving versus captive furnace oil, LDO or natural gas is 25% to 35%, while coal-fired large textile users may be only at par.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed to reach 705 TPH and when will projects go live?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crore more for the four under-construction projects, targeted to go live in FY27. Another INR170 crore over 15-18 months for IPO-funded and Tarapur projects; Tarapur 60 TPH by Q4 FY28, Dahej/Ankleshwar/Panoli by Q1 FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is utilisation of 41% consistent with the planned ramp, and where does the company target it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 60%-65% utilisation; newer boilers are expected to run at about 50% in initial months after commissioning. Some capacity is held back for 2-3 years of new demand.

qa_highlights.question: What are receivable days and CFO to EBITDA ratio, and what are the related-party steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing?
qa_highlights.answer: Fortnightly billing with payments typically 7th to 15th day. Operating cash flow was about 1.2 times EBITDA last time, expected to hold or be slightly lower. Steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing for the Sachin location continue for at least the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected on the Una project and what is the revenue-share structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 8%-10% clear margin per ton, passed through to end consumers, with no capex. The 9% revenue share to Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Ltd is to be recovered from steam customers. Agreement not yet signed.

qa_highlights.question: What is a sustainable volume growth rate and can company-level 20%-25% volume growth be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 5%-10% growth at existing locations, with new capacity adding further. CFO said 20%-25% company-level volume growth is achievable 'very comfortably'.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR1,000 EBITDA per ton sustainable, and what about Q2 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA per ton of about INR1,000 is expected to hold for the next few quarters, with Q2 an exception due to monsoon. Structural changes cited: coal purchases moved from credit to cash, solar power installed, inventory optimisation. Full-year to be at par or better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there government interest in community boilers and are more such opportunities in the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to Bulk Drug Park and PM MITRA Park schemes from 2021-22 and a March 2024 CPCB guideline pushing SMEs to common boilers. Gujarat Bulk Drug Park tender is live; PM MITRA and Textile Ministry discussions are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did steam revenue rise 46% when volume rose 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation improved from better utilisation and asset leverage, plus higher waste-to-energy usage at Vapi. Growth also came from chemical and pharma recovery and new tyre and food processing (Haldia) customers.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital guidance and cash purchases?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle guided at 35-40 days positive. Coal was bought on credit until May 2026 and has since moved entirely to cash purchases, which management said lowers fuel cost.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split between own-generated and traded steam, and margin split by business?
qa_highlights.answer: Own-boiler steam was 73.7% of Q1 revenue and traded steam 22.2%. Management declined to split margins between generation and trading, citing competitive sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA CAGR guidance of 30%-35% going to be beaten?

qa_highlights.answer: Management does not break out AI revenue. It said every project includes AI, and pure AI work is limited to AI co-innovation labs.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from the US and how will it change?
qa_highlights.answer: US share is 52% (management corrected from 55%), with a target of at least 65% in two to three years.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 is expected to be muted, and FY27 guidance of INR 1,200-1,250 crore requires a sharp H2 recovery from a flat H1.
Deal conversion is slow as the shift to larger outcome-based deals lengthens decision cycles.
Digital commerce faces the most headwinds, and BFSI revenue is flat QoQ.
Management did not quantify the number of accounts exited; it promised to send figures later. Pipeline figure of USD 28 million is also to be confirmed in writing.
Long-term INR 500 million target (FY30) was raised by an analyst but not addressed by management.
Competition from larger IT players moving down into smaller deals.
Appraisals next quarter could push up employee costs.
590051|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious on near-term demand and conversion, with management openly saying Q2 will be muted and that they do not expect improvement soon. It is more confident on the medium-term pipeline, AI productivity and the move to managed services, but it gave few hard numbers beyond the FY27 guidance it reiterated.
key_quotes: Decision making is getting delayed unfortunately, and we are pushing as hard as we can, but there is a limit to how much you can fight the industry
Numbers will come, growth will come, it won't happen overnight.
Nothing is normalizing.
Nothing is pilot, everything is in production.
